contracts.description: Meeting & Conference Platform HTTP API (/api/v1, /api/v2). 1.2.0 (Part VI §51): platformCredential (meetings.read / meetings.write, x-cfmeet-required-scope) on the machine-callable /api/v2 operations — meeting spaces, instant meetings, conference scheduling and lifecycle, participants and waiting room, invitations, attendance — for meetings owned by the caller's application environment. 1.3.0 (Blueprint Section 16): legacy webhook and v1 create operations deprecated (Deprecation / Sunset headers, delivery NOT_DELIVERED), optional request bodies not required, UTC timestamps. 1.4.0 (Blueprint Sections 2-3 hardening): optional DeactivateAccountRequest on POST /api/v1/users/me/deactivate (current password or a recent sign-in, 403 REAUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED), error codes REAUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED and EMAIL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED, legacy API keys masked by their lookup prefix and never stored, legacy webhook secrets never stored, legacy kick evicts media; no operation added or removed. 1.6.0 (Notification Service N8, Document 4 §3.1): the nine Notification Service user operations U1–U9 under /api/v2/notifications (inbox list, unread count with ETag / 304, item update, mark read, dismiss, preferences read / update, push endpoint register / remove; tag Notifications (v2)), relayed by the Meeting Service with the server-resolved account to I2 dispatchNotificationsUser; answers are the Notification Service's own (schemaVersion 1, Retry-After and ETag relayed); 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE until CF_NOTIFICATIONS_BASE_URL is configured. 1.7.0 (gap audit G3): an organization member's own calling presence in the organization's own Calling scope (tag Organizations (v2)): GET / POST /api/v2/organizations/{id}/member-calling/endpoints, DELETE /api/v2/organizations/{id}/member-calling/endpoints/{endpointId} and POST /api/v2/organizations/{id}/member-calling/signaling-credentials, acting as the member's organization principal (active membership and features.calling; no administrative capability); 409 ORGANIZATION_CALLING_DISABLED unless ORGANIZATION_CALLING_SCOPE=organization. 1.8.0 (ADR 0067, signing in is enough on the web): POST /api/v2/me/devices/current trusts a WEB device declared from a fresh sign-in (trustedVia BOOTSTRAP; an untrusted browser declaring again with its key is trusted the same way) and, at maxWebDevices, revokes the least recently used browser instead of answering 409 WEB_DEVICE_LIMIT_REACHED; a new MOBILE is unchanged (REPLACEMENT_PENDING until a link completes); no operation, schema or error code added or removed. 1.9.0 (server audit, meetings): POST /api/v2/conferences/{id}/extend (ExtendConferenceRequest; host / co-host extends a live conference, realtime conference.extended, and conference.ending_soon 5 minutes before every automatic end); the private calendar feed GET / POST / DELETE /api/v2/me/calendar-feed (CalendarFeedResponse) and the public GET /api/v2/calendar-feeds/{file} (token-authenticated iCalendar); RegistrationCreated.emailDelivery and an idempotent registration repeat returning the same admission token (409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT for a different request under the same key).

HTTP surface exposed by the Calling service: health, the call API (list, get, available actions), application call creation and control (accept, decline, cancel, end, hold, resume, transfer, session removal, media credentials), the endpoint registry, signaling-credential minting, the endpoint's signaling operations (WebSocket channel, offer recovery, accept / decline, media credentials), the media connection gateway (admission before every media connection) and the media provider callback; the platform credential, signaling credential, media credential and provider signature schemes; the error envelope. No generic state mutation. Protected calls (privacyRelaySessionId, PRIVACY_RELAY_V1, fail closed: PRIVACY_AUTHORIZATION_UNAVAILABLE) and the internal Privacy Relay enforcement route (POST /internal/v1/privacy-relay/enforcement). The public Privacy Relay API served by this ingress is specified by cfmeet.privacy-relay.http-api. Part E: protected public-network contact targets on POST /v1/calls (APP_TO_PSTN; PUBLIC_ROUTE_DENIED / PUBLIC_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE / TELECOM_SPEND_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) the callback relay (callbackRequested on POST /v1/calls) and the internal Telephony event receiver (POST /internal/v1/telephony/events). Part F: the enterprise calling API under /v1/enterprise/** (policies, departments, extensions, ring groups, queues, IVR, business hours, forwarding, voicemail, recording policies, audit; enterprise.* scopes, expectedVersion, VERSION_CONFLICT / ENTERPRISE_POLICY_DENIED) and enterprise call targets. 1.9.0 DCN inbound offers (POST /internal/v1/telephony/dcn-inbound-calls) and presentedNumberResourceId (Part IV L); 1.10.0 the SMS Gateway as a platform-event producer (sms.* webhooks, Part IV N). 1.11.0 Messaging as a platform-event producer (conversation.* / message.* webhooks, Part V I). 1.12.0 the Part VI §53 webhook migration export (webhook-migration.export; secrets only transfer-sealed) and rollback (webhook-migration.import) internal routes; CF-Webhook-Migration frozen / moved refusals. 1.13.0 the preserved service-specific usage / limit views GET /v1/calling/usage and GET /v1/calling/limits (Part VI §19.4). 1.15.0 Blueprint §12: GET /v1/enterprise/recordings (scope-wide recording discovery, filtered and keyset-paginated, access-audited; CAL-017) and the signaling channel's 4401 close on a revoked endpoint (ACC-024). 1.16.0 (Blueprint Section 12 follow-up, CAL-007): enterprise audit records carry actorPrincipalId — the acting human principal of a first-party organization request Meeting Service forwarded (null for a plain platform credential). 1.18.0 (Calling gap closure C16): GET /v1/enterprise/voicemail/mailboxes filters by owner (ownerType, ownerId). 1.19.0 (C5): createAbuseReport specifies its body and takes reportedPrincipalId (the reported participant of a call of more than two people; another participant of that call). 1.20.0 (C8): POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/sessions/{session_id}/quality-samples (jitter, packet loss, RTT; server-estimated MOS) and GET /v1/calls/{call_id}/quality (per-participant aggregates). 1.21.0 (C4): the call host - POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/host (transfer), host-only end / hold / resume for everyone in a group call (actingParticipantId), POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/participants/{participant_id}/remove and /mute, and hostParticipantId / mutedParticipantIds on the Call. 1.22.0 (C6): POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/participants/{participant_id}/rejoin (rejoin an ongoing call unless removed by the host). 1.23.0 (C7): the recording notice and consent apply to participants who join after a recording started (notice at once, consent within 60 s or the recording stops). 1.24.0 (C13): DELETE /v1/calls/{call_id}/history?principalId= (hide a finished call from one's own history) and the CALL_HISTORY retention purge (default 400 days). 1.25.0 (C3): forwarding rules (ALWAYS / UNAVAILABLE / BUSY / NO_ANSWER) and the callee's own mailbox as voicemail fallback apply to direct one-to-one application calls. 1.26.0 (C21): internal operator review of abuse reports (listAbuseReportsForReview, resolveAbuseReport; permission calling-abuse-reports.review, operator console only). 1.27.0 (C15): queue wrap-up time (wrapUpSeconds) honoured in queue distribution and QUEUE transfer-target selection, and built-in queue hold music (holdMusic) on createQueue / updateQueue / the Queue view and the queued caller's Call. 1.28.0 (C14): attended (consultative) transfer - POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/consultations (hold the call and place a consultation call to the target), POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/consultations/{consultation_id}/complete (the canonical transfer of the original call to the consulted target; the consultation call ends when the target joined) and /cancel (end the consultation call, resume the original); a transfer that started from HELD lifts the hold at the media provider when it completes. 1.29.0 (gap audit G3): organization member endpoints, signaling credentials and extension status over internal service authentication (calling-organization-member.act / .offboard, Meeting Service only). 1.30.0 (CF Meet Platform): POST /v1/calling/user-sessions (CF Meet user token exchange for a partner device; ADR 0062). 1.31.0: a target already in a live call is not rung and a Call whose every target is on another call ends BUSY at once (CF1); upgrade to VIDEO also while DIALING / RINGING (CF2); cancel and end answer before the media cleanup (C1). 1.32.0 (S2, account deletion and data download): POST /internal/v1/account-privacy/erasure and /export over internal service authentication (calling-account.privacy, Meeting Service only): erase (hide from history, minimize display names) or export the call history of a deleted or exporting account's principal in the delegated CF Meet FIRST_PARTY scope. 1.34.0 (ADR 0068, admin bridge): operator attribution (X-CF-Operator and the approval headers) accepted only from cfmeet.admin-bridge and refused on every internal route from any other caller; the admin bridge's tenant-scoped operator reads under /internal/v1/operator/* (calls, live calls, abuse reports, block rules, limits, routing, enterprise and spend policies, recording and voicemail metadata, retention holds, incidents, webhook sealing keys, operator audit), each requiring calling.administer and X-CF-Operator.

Canonical call-domain vocabulary (Part C sections 15-25): the 17 call states, call kind, normalized failure categories, terminal reasons, participant roles, session states, endpoint categories, call event types, the call representation (CallCore / CallSummary), ring-offer, media-access, transfer and endpoint vocabularies, server-authorized media capabilities and the bounded safe event data object. Part F: VOICEMAIL_RECEIVED / VOICEMAIL_READY / VOICEMAIL_DELETED call events. Part F: ENTERPRISE_ROUTING_STEP call events (durable enterprise routing evidence).

Payload of every call event published through Calling's transactional outbox inside the cfmeet.platform.event-envelope: ids, scope, gap-free sequence, call version, states, time, correlation id and safe data. Provider-independent; no telephone numbers, provider ids, credentials or tokens.

Request and response bodies of the application-calling API (Part C sections 20-25): call creation, ring-offer answers, cancel / end / hold / resume / transfer and their results, session removal, available actions, the ring-offer and transfer representations, media credentials, endpoints, signaling credentials and offer recovery. No client-chosen scope, state, permission or provider data; no provider identifiers or administrative capabilities in responses. Part F: enterprise extension targets, enterprise transfer targets and the enterprise context of created calls. 1.5.0 presentedNumberResourceId: present an entitled Digital Communications Number on a protected-contact call (Part IV L). 1.7.0 (C8): QualitySampleRequest, QualitySampleResult and CallQualitySummary. 1.8.0 (C4): actingParticipantId on CommandRequest, TransferHostRequest, HostActionRequest, MuteParticipantRequest and HostControlResult. 1.9.0 (C6): RejoinRequest and RejoinResult. 1.10.0 (C14): ConsultationRequest, Consultation, ConsultationResult, ConsultationCompleteRequest, ConsultationCompletion and ConsultationCancelResult.

Frames of an endpoint's realtime signaling channel: call signals (call.incoming ... call.invitation_expired) derived from committed state and sent after commit, with event id, call id, version / sequence, target endpoint and principal, safe state, issue time, offer expiry, correlation id and a bounded payload; and the channel control frames. No telephone numbers, provider ids, credentials or tokens. Part F: call.queued and call.queue_position (to the caller of a queued enterprise Call; data queueId, position). call.ivr_waiting / call.ivr_input (to the caller of a Call in an IVR; never the key pressed). Part F: call.recording_started (the server-issued recording notice) and call.recording_stopped. Part F: call.voicemail_started (the caller is now leaving a message). Part G: call.route_changed (a public leg failed over to another route on the same Call; data failover only). 1.4.0 (C14): call.consultation_transfer (on a consultation call, to its parties: the original call is being transferred to the consulted target; data consultationId, originalCallId, transferId).

Transport-neutral push-ready payload of a ring offer (call id, offer id, call kind, optional caller display name, issue and expiry times) for a future push service. No media credential, provider token, API credential or telephone number.

Enterprise calling bodies (Part F sections 52-62): enterprise call policy, departments, extensions, ring groups, call queues and queue entries, IVR flows and versions, business hours, forwarding rules, voicemail mailboxes and messages, call-recording policies, authorizations and recordings, administrative audit and the safe enterprise call context. Never a raw telephone number, provider / SIP identifier, DTMF digits, object key or public URL. 1.1.0 (Blueprint Section 12 follow-up, CAL-007): AuditRecord gains actorPrincipalId (required, nullable uuid). 1.2.0 (C15): queues carry wrapUpSeconds (0-600; an agent is not offered another of the queue's calls until it has passed since their previous call answered from the queue ended) and holdMusic (HoldMusicRef: a BuiltinHoldMusic DEFAULT / CALM / BRIGHT, or null); EnterpriseQueueState.holdMusic shows it to the waiting caller.

Shared definitions: service identity, runtime environment, request/correlation ids, UUIDs, application environment kind, principal kind, key ids, internal permissions. Part F: internal permissions telephony-leg.media (Calling -> Telephony: answer / built-in prompt / capture of internal enterprise SIP legs) telephony-enterprise.offer (Telephony -> Calling: internal enterprise SIP dialog offers and keypad input) and telephony-capture.deliver (Telephony -> Calling: edge media captures — voicemail / recording audio with integrity metadata). Part IV: platform-credential.authenticate, platform-principal.resolve, platform-principal.register, platform-identity.read and platform-identity.administer (received by Platform Access) and number-resource.read (received by Numbering). Numbering routing grant permissions (number-route.resolve, number-caller-identity.authorize, number-sms-sender.authorize, number-grant.verify). 1.8.0 number-sms-route.resolve (Part IV M). 1.9.0 number-usage.report, number-risk.report and number-relay.lease (Part IV S, T and P §§119–120). 1.9.1 cfmeet.messaging named as a service identity (Part V A). 1.10.0 (Part VI): service identities cfmeet.developer-platform and cfmeet.api-gateway; permission developer-request.forward. 1.12.0 (Part VI §51): permission meeting-request.forward (API Gateway -> Meeting Service platform-credential meetings requests). 1.13.0 (Blueprint Sections 3-5): service identity cfmeet.organizations; permissions organization.read, organization.write, organization.act-for-user, organization.administer and organization.migrate (received by Organizations). 1.14.0 (Blueprint Section 7, ADR 0058): permission platform-identity.provision-first-party (received by Platform Access, grantable to cfmeet.organizations only, sensitive). 1.15.0 (Blueprint Section 12 follow-up, CAL-007): permission calling-request.act-for-organization (received by Calling, grantable to cfmeet.meeting-service only, sensitive). 1.16.0 (final closure, organization event delivery): permission meeting-organization-events.apply (received by the Meeting Service, grantable to cfmeet.organizations only). 1.17.0 (ADR 0058 Amendment A2, automatic organization service bindings): permission platform-identity.bind-organization-services (received by Platform Access, grantable to cfmeet.organizations only, sensitive). 1.18.0 (Notification Service blueprint, roadmap N1; owner decision D-13): service identity cfmeet.notifications and twelve permissions — received by cfmeet.notifications: notifications-event.publish (Meeting Service, Organizations, Communications, Calling, Messaging, Developer Platform), notifications-user.forward (Meeting Service), notifications-call-push.dispatch (Calling), notifications-observability.read, notifications-operations.replay (sensitive), notifications-operations.reroute (sensitive) (operator console); granted only to cfmeet.notifications: account-contacts.read (Meeting Service, sensitive), meeting-notification-recipients.read (Meeting Service, sensitive), messaging-wakeups.authorize (Messaging), communications-restrictions.read (Communications), organization-invitations.read (Organizations), account-route-lease.claim (Meeting Service). 1.19.0 (Notification Service roadmap N10, preference move): permission communications-preferences.export (received by Communications, grantable to cfmeet.notifications only, sensitive: the one-off preference copy and change-feed catch-up); notifications-user.forward is also grantable to cfmeet.communications (the Hub preference facade over U6 / U7; the service accepts only U6 / U7 from the Hub). Also in 1.19.0 (Notification Service roadmap N9, D-1b copy path): permission notifications-push-registration.sync (received by cfmeet.notifications, grantable to cfmeet.messaging only; carries push handles, sealed at rest by the receiver; the copy and facade of Messaging push registrations of CF Meet first-party accounts). 1.20.0 (Calling C21): permission calling-abuse-reports.review (received by cfmeet.calling, grantable to cfmeet.operator-console only, sensitive): operator list / resolve of abuse reports. 1.21.0 (gap audit G3): permissions calling-organization-member.act (received by cfmeet.calling, grantable to cfmeet.meeting-service only, sensitive: an organization member's own endpoints and signaling credentials in the organization scope) and calling-organization-member.offboard (received by cfmeet.calling, grantable to cfmeet.meeting-service only: disable / restore the extensions routed to a removed, suspended or reactivated member). 1.22.0 (CF Meet Platform Build, ADRs 0062 / 0063): platform-end-users.delegate and notifications-push-provider.manage (Developer Console only), platform-user-token.verify (Messaging, Calling, Meeting Service, API Gateway), platform-environment-origins.read (API Gateway, Messaging, Calling, Meeting Service), platform-principal.ensure-meeting-platform (Meeting Service only, sensitive) and messaging-meeting.sync-platform (Meeting Service only); CF Meet Apps (ADRs 0064 / 0065): platform-oauth.manage and platform-oauth.token (Developer Console only), platform-oauth.authorize (Meeting Service only, sensitive), organization-apps.evaluate (Meeting Service only) and meeting-oauth-userinfo.read (Developer Console only). 1.23.0 (S2): calling-account.privacy. 1.24.0 (HQ admin bridge, ADR 0068): service identity cfmeet.admin-bridge (the only doorway from the CosmicForge central admin; owns no business data, never reads E2EE content) and nine permissions — operator permissions grantable to cfmeet.admin-bridge only, sensitive, each requiring X-CF-Operator (and X-CF-Approver, a different person, for R3 / R4 actions): account.administer and meeting.administer (received by the Meeting Service), messaging-firstparty.administer (Messaging), calling.administer (Calling), communications.administer (Communications), organization.operator-read (Organizations), pricing.administer (Developer Platform) and notifications.administer (Notification Service); hq-bridge-events.publish (received by cfmeet.admin-bridge, grantable to the Meeting Service, Messaging, Calling, Communications, Organizations, Developer Platform, Platform Access and the Notification Service; owner events with ids, states and versions only). The existing operator permissions calling-abuse-reports.review, communications-profile.suspend, organization.administer, developer-platform.administer, platform-identity.administer, notifications-observability.read, notifications-operations.replay and notifications-operations.reroute are also grantable to cfmeet.admin-bridge (existing grantees unchanged).
JOSE header of internal service tokens (EdDSA pinned).
Claims of internal service tokens: issuer, exact audience, runtime environment, short lifetime, token id, signed request and correlation ids, optional delegated context.
Safe customer/application/actor identifiers carried inside a signed service token.
Receiver-controlled trust policy: trusted issuers, Ed25519 public keys and locally granted internal permissions.
Internal service-to-service HTTP conventions: service auth security scheme, request/correlation headers, normalized internal auth errors.

Envelope for durable cross-service events. Payload contracts are registered separately by the producing service (Calling: cfmeet.calling.call-lifecycle-event; Privacy Relay: cfmeet.privacy-relay.event).

Customer webhooks (Part G §68): application-scoped subscriptions (create / list / get / update / delete / rotate-secret), the safe subscription view (the signing secret is returned only on create / rotation), delivery records with dead-letter visibility and manual replay, and the normalized, signed event body (public catalog projected from committed domain events; never a provider or internal payload). Served by Calling's platform ingress. Part IV: 1.1.0 sms.received (N); 1.2.0 sms.requested / submitted / delivered / failed / unknown / blocked (O) from the SMS Gateway (references, status and codes only; never content or a number). Part V I: 1.3.0 conversation.created / updated / member_added / member_removed and message.created / deleted / moderated / expired from Messaging (ids, sequences and codes only; never message content of any security profile). 1.4.0 (Calling gap closure C11): call.kind_changed, call.screen_share_started / call.screen_share_stopped and call.participant_added (calls.read) and recording.started / recording.stopped / recording.failed (enterprise.recording.read) from Calling (ids and codes only).

Usage and limits (Part G §69 / §70): the ledger of final consumption facts of the authenticated application environment (application media, public-network legs with KNOWN / ESTIMATED / UNKNOWN cost evidence, stored voicemail / recording artifacts — never a bill) and the limit status (request rate, concurrent calls, telecom spend) with every level of the API-client chain (tenant → application → service account → credential), the independent principal axis of a principal resolved in the caller's scope, and the binding level. Served by Calling's platform ingress.

Messages of the shared identity authority (Part IV Workstream B, ADR 0032): identity snapshots (tenant, application, environment, service account, credential WITHOUT verifier material, principal, scopes), credential authentication outcomes with the trusted authority chain and throttling, the trusted delegated context, credential status, authorization evaluation, the scope registry (Calling, Numbering and SMS scopes; PRIVILEGED_OPERATOR trust for numbers.admin), the commit-ordered identity change feed, Part III import receipts, principal resolution / telephone-endpoint registration / first-party principal ensure (Part V H §104) / tombstones and the error envelope. 1.2.0: principals/ensure also accepts BOT_OR_SERVICE (a first-party application's own non-human participant, e.g. the system owner of meeting breakout / private chat conversations). 1.3.0: credential SUSPENDED effective state and the credential_suspended rejection reason (Part VI §54). 1.5.0 (CF Meet Platform): partner user-token and OAuth error codes, OAuth authority fields (credentialKind, appId, grantId, restrictedPrincipal, credentialIssuedAt) (ADR 0062/0064). 1.6.0 (ADR 0068): error code VERSION_CONFLICT.

Internal HTTP surface of services/platform-access: GET /health, GET /ready and the service-authenticated /internal/v1 API — credential authentication, credential status, authorization evaluation, trusted context, identity change feed, import receipts, scope registry, principal resolution / registration / tombstone (Calling, Numbering), first-party principal ensure (Meeting Service, Part V H §104) and operator administration (operator console, audited). 1.4.0: Developer Platform delegation of service accounts (create / list / read / suspend / resume in non-production environments; never credentials). 1.5.0: Part VI §54 / §55 delegated credentials, suspension, scope grants, production activation and live telecom. 1.6.0 (Blueprint Section 7, ADR 0058): governed FIRST_PARTY organization scopes for the Organizations Service (platform-identity.provision-first-party): idempotent create-or-return, read-back and tenant suspension / resumption. 1.7.0 (Blueprint Section 15): operator-only paginated read of the operator audit trail (GET /internal/v1/admin/audit, PLT-009), delegated EXTERNAL tenant rename (ORG-013) and creation-slug lookup for organization-creation reconciliation (ORG-014); credential views add lastAuthenticatedAt and expiringSoon (PLT-008). 1.9.0 (ADR 0058 Amendment A2): automatic organization service bindings (platform-identity.bind-organization-services, Organizations only): create-or-return / renew, read-back, rotate and revoke of an organization's Calling / Messaging service account and credential inside its own FIRST_PARTY triple; the secret is never returned. 1.12.0 (CF Meet Platform): partner end users, user tokens, environment origins, meeting platform principals, console test tokens (1.10.0-1.11.0, ADR 0062); OAuth clients, authorization, tokens, grants (1.12.0, ADR 0064). 1.13.0 (ADR 0068): the admin bridge's read-only operator views under /internal/v1/operator/* (tenants, applications, environments, service accounts, scope grants, API keys, principals, allowed websites, identity-record search, OAuth apps and grants, audit; platform-identity.administer and the bridge's hq: operator; never a secret, verifier or external reference) and operator attribution accepted only from the admin bridge (and the legacy named operator from the operator console). 1.14.0 (ADR 0068 A4): the admin bridge's identity commands under POST /internal/v1/operator/* (status changes, scope grants, API key revoke / suspend / resume, identity records, app grants, allowed websites, partner-user sign-out; Idempotency-Key, expectedVersion, two-person approval, recorded in platform_access_admin_operations) and the settlement read GET /internal/v1/operator/operations/{idempotencyKey}; never a key issue or rotation. 1.14.0 (ADR 0068 A4): the admin bridge's identity commands under POST /internal/v1/operator/* (status changes, scope grants, API key revoke / suspend / resume, identity records, app grants, allowed websites, partner-user sign-out; Idempotency-Key, expectedVersion, two-person approval, recorded in platform_access_admin_operations) and the settlement read GET /internal/v1/operator/operations/{idempotencyKey}. 1.15.0 (ADR 0068 A4, owner-delivered secrets): identity.key.issue / identity.key.rotate through the bridge answer the delivery reference only; the secret is sealed for one reveal in the partner's Developer Platform console (delegation: list pending deliveries, reveal once; destroyed at the reveal, after 7 days or on revocation).

The canonical Numbering vocabulary and messages (Part IV C5, ADR 0033): Number Resource identity (CF Meet ids canonical, provider identifiers never exposed), type, capabilities with provenance, opaque provider binding references, inventory observations, reservations, DCN assignments with ownership and routing references, routing profiles, lifecycle transitions, the trusted context and the error envelope; 1.1.0 the capability and country catalog (E); 1.2.0 KYC requirements, cases, protected evidence metadata, decisions, appeals and eligibility decisions (F); 1.3.0 provider command, provider event and incident vocabularies and the provider callback acknowledgement (G). 1.4.0 inventory search results / pages with freshness, KYC indicators, country and number-type lists, reservation creation / list, hold basis and conversion, RELEASE_HOLD commands (H). 1.5.0 acquisitions, route families / configurations / readiness (I). 1.6.0 ownership and assignment requests / views, routing target kinds, pools and transfer links (J). 1.7.0 routing grant rule codes (K). 1.8.0 lifecycle stewardship messages (P–X): suspensions, releases, quarantines, reassignment, usage, risk decisions and appeals, port requests, access justification / ownership periods / verification, operational controls, reconciliation report, usage / risk-signal reports and relay import / lease / resolution (Part P); new domain rules.

Numbering domain events in the platform envelope (transactional outbox, at least once, per-aggregate order): resource discovered / lifecycle-changed / classified, binding changed, capability changed, reservation changed, assignment changed, routing profile revised, catalog revised, KYC requirements published, KYC case changed, KYC evidence received, eligibility evaluated, provider command changed, provider event received. No telephone number, provider identifier, credential or secret; 1.4.0 RELEASE_HOLD provider commands (H); 1.5.0 acquisition changed, route changed (I); 1.6.0 pool changed (J). 1.7.0 number.suspended, number.restored, release / quarantine / usage / risk / port / relay-lease changes (P–X).

HTTP surface of services/numbering: GET /health, /ready, /openapi.json (the served contract); customer reads of the caller's own DCN assignments / history / reservations, the catalog, KYC / eligibility (F); 1.4.0 provider-neutral inventory search, countries and number types, reservations (create with Idempotency-Key, list, cancel) (H); 1.5.0 acquisitions (provisioning with eligibility re-evaluation and hold read-back) and provider route configuration (I); provider callbacks (G); and the service-authenticated internal Number Resource view (/internal/v1, number-resource.read). 1.5.0 internal route view and consumer route readiness (number-route.acknowledge). 1.6.0 ownership and assignment: assignment creation / activation on proven readiness, routing revisions, employee offboarding, same-owner transfers, organizational pools and the operator assignment history (J). 1.7.0 routing grants: inbound resolution (number-route.resolve), caller-identity / SMS-sender grants (delegated scope) and authoritative verification (number-grant.verify) (K). 1.8.0 delegated current-assignment view for Calling's caller-identity policy (L). 1.9.0 dedicated SMS destination resolver (number-sms-route.resolve); inbound-resolutions is voice only (M); 1.10.0 the SMS Gateway's sender re-check on number-assignments (Part IV O). 1.11.0 inventoryClass on voice inbound resolutions, grant verifications and current-assignment views (L closure: synthetic test interconnects). 1.12.0 lifecycle stewardship (P–X) and the relay-number import / lease / resolution API (Part P). 1.13.0 x-cfmeet-required-scope (the API Gateway scope pre-check) on the 51 customer operations whose handler requires exactly one registry scope; GET /v1/numbers/catalog/countries/{countryCode} accepts numbers.search OR numbers.read and stays upstream-checked (Section 15, PLT-011).

Number routing grants (Part IV Workstream K): inbound resolution, caller-identity / SMS-sender grant requests and verification bodies, the grant claims (typ cf-number-grant+jwt, Numbering's dedicated grant key, no telephone number, revision-bound) and the receiver-authoritative grant trust bundle. 1.1.0 CurrentAssignment (L). 1.2.0 SmsDestinationResolutionRequest (M). 1.3.0 inventoryClass (SYNTHETIC / REAL) on voice resolutions, valid verifications and the current-assignment view (L closure). 1.4.0 ROUTING_DISABLED (an operator kill switch, Workstream W).

The CF Meet Privacy Relay API (Part D sections 26-30): Communication Contexts (create, list, get, typed versioned update / participant reassignment, suspend, resume, complete, revoke, privacy-safe evidence) and Privacy Relay Sessions (create, list, get, suspend, resume, revoke). Served by the authenticated platform ingress; Privacy Relay is the business and data authority. One generic model for first-party and external applications; no telephone numbers, providers, Contact Vault material or credentials.
